caption: An observer watches the bottom cane block: it fires at every growth step and when the cane grows. Its pulse reaches the piston through a stone and the dust on it; the piston head breaks the cane's second block and shoves the item into a hopper minecart standing on the hopper (no rail), which takes every item at once (a hopper waits 8 gt after each item it takes); the hopper under it empties it into the chest. Water: a waterlogged waxed copper grate beside the soil. Copies stand side by side, 5 apart.

Two canes share one observer and one wire. The observer watches the east cane's bottom block (it fires at every growth step) and powers, through a stone and the dust on it, both pistons, one on each side of the dust: each pushes into its cane's second block, and the head shoves the item into a hopper minecart standing on that cane's hopper (a cart takes every item at once). The west cane is harvested at the east cane's next growth step. Water: a waterlogged waxed copper grate beside each soil. Copies stand side by side.

Four canes share one observer, one wire and two water blocks. The observer watches the east cane's bottom block (it fires at every growth step) and powers, through a stone and the dust on it, four pistons, one on each arm of the dust: each pushes into its cane's second block, and the head shoves the item into a hopper minecart standing on that cane's hopper (a cart takes every item at once). The other canes are harvested at the east cane's next growth step. Water: one waterlogged waxed copper grate touches three soils, another the fourth.

Kelp planted on a hopper. An observer watches the bottom kelp, which turns from kelp to kelp_plant when the kelp grows a block: its pulse powers the stone behind it, whose dust climbs onto a wall to the piston above the second block. The piston pushes down into the second block: it breaks it and pushes the item down into the bottom block's cell, where the hopper below takes it (kelp has no collision, and the hopper reaches through it). A water source beside the second block refills it; an item the piston head squeezes out into that water floats up to its surface, where a second hopper under the source takes it. Copies stand side by side, 4 blocks apart.

An observer above the stem watches it: when a pumpkin grows beside the stem, the stem turns to an attached stem and the observer fires into the dust on its top. The dust's power reaches the cell above the piston, which stands above the fruit's cell facing down (a piston is also powered through the cell above it), and the dust's update reaches the piston: it pushes down, breaks the pumpkin and presses the item onto the mud. Mud is lower than a full block, so a hopper minecart under the mud reaches the item, and it takes it before the squeezed item can shoot sideways (a minecart ticks with the entities, before the item moves); the hopper under the minecart empties it into the chest. The stem's other three sides have nothing below them, so the pumpkin only grows on the mud. Copies stand side by side, 2 blocks apart.

An observer above the stem watches it: when a melon grows beside the stem, the stem turns to an attached stem and the observer fires into the dust on its top. The dust's power reaches the cell above the piston, which stands above the fruit's cell facing down (a piston is also powered through the cell above it), and the dust's update reaches the piston: it pushes down, breaks the melon and presses its slices (one stack) onto the mud. Mud is lower than a full block, so a hopper minecart under the mud reaches them, and it takes them before the squeezed stack can shoot sideways (a minecart ticks with the entities, before the item moves); the hopper under the minecart empties it into the chest. The stem's other three sides have nothing below them, so the melon only grows on the mud. Copies stand side by side, 2 blocks apart.

A piston beside the cactus's second cell, a sculk sensor beside the piston, a wool block above that cell and a stone on each of its two other sides. The piston and the stones are solid, so a cactus block that grows into that cell breaks itself a tick later; the sensor hears the block break (a vibration) and powers the piston for 30 ticks: the head sweeps the cell and shoves the cactus item (a cactus item touching a cactus dies in 5 ticks; the stones and the wool keep it inside the head's sweep) into the cell beyond, where a hopper minecart standing on a hopper takes it at once; the hopper empties it into the chest. Items landing on wool make no vibration, so things falling onto the farm do not keep the sensor busy. A stone holds up the sand. Copies stand 9 blocks apart (a sensor hears 8 blocks around it).

Four pumpkin stems around one fruit cell, each on its own farmland; the cell is on mud and each stem's other sides have nothing below them, so every pumpkin grows in that cell. An observer above each stem watches it (a stem turns to an attached stem when its pumpkin grows) and fires into the dust on its top; each dust powers the cell above the piston, which stands above the fruit's cell facing down (a piston is also powered through the cell above it), and the dust's update reaches the piston: it breaks the pumpkin and presses the item onto the mud, lower than a full block, where a hopper minecart under the mud takes it before the squeezed item can shoot sideways; the hopper under the minecart empties it into the chest. Copies stand side by side, 3 blocks apart.

Four melon stems around one fruit cell, each on its own farmland; the cell is on mud and each stem's other sides have nothing below them, so every melon grows in that cell. An observer above each stem watches it (a stem turns to an attached stem when its melon grows) and fires into the dust on its top; each dust powers the cell above the piston, which stands above the fruit's cell facing down (a piston is also powered through the cell above it), and the dust's update reaches the piston: it breaks the melon and presses its slices (one stack) onto the mud, lower than a full block, where a hopper minecart under the mud takes them before the squeezed stack can shoot sideways; the hopper under the minecart empties it into the chest. Copies stand side by side, 3 blocks apart.

An observer watches the bamboo's third block; its pulse lights the dust behind it, whose stone powers the piston below the observer: the piston breaks the second block and the third block falls. A hopper minecart stands on the mud inside the stalk (the bamboo grows through it; a minecart takes items from the cell above it up to most of the second block): it takes the second block's item and anything that reaches the stump. A second hopper minecart stands half on a hopper beside the stalk, half over the third block's cell: it takes the third block's item as it appears and any item lying on the second block, and that hopper empties it into a chest. Walls keep items over the stalk; a stone caps it. Copies stand side by side, 3 blocks apart.

A melon stem with a fruit cell on all four sides and wet farmland on its diagonals: it rolls 1 in 4 instead of 1 in 13 and every roll grows a melon; the observer's dust fires four downward pistons, and each cell's slices go through the mud into a hopper minecart

A pumpkin stem with a fruit cell on all four sides and wet farmland on its diagonals: it rolls 1 in 4 instead of 1 in 13 and every roll grows a pumpkin; the observer's dust fires four downward pistons, and each cell's pumpkin goes through the mud into a hopper minecart

A bamboo harvester one block wide (1x6x4): bamboo-hc-12b's mechanism (an observer on the bamboo's third block fires the piston below it, which breaks the second block so the third falls; hopper minecarts take the items into a chest) rearranged by clk-rt's circuit compact (2026-10-21) on the full farm twin: judged box 24 (was 72), 10 blocks (was 12), the same yield (16.79 items per hour per cane, the seed 16.78); robust in the game.

64 melon stems two blocks apart on wet farmland, with a fruit cell on mud between every two stems (each stem has four, each shared with a neighbour) and wet farmland on every diagonal, so every stem grows at the fastest rate (a melon every 4 tries). An observer over each stem fires the four pistons over its fruit cells; the squeezed melon drops into a hopper minecart under the mud, and a hopper line under each pair of rows carries the slices to a chest (8 chests). Needs open sky or light 9 at the stems. The carts go in with the rail trick (rail, cart, break the rail). 2112 iron. Copies side by side every 17 blocks; a bigger square comes close to 5 slices an hour per block.

64 pumpkin stems two blocks apart on wet farmland, with a fruit cell on mud between every two stems (each stem has four, each shared with a neighbour) and wet farmland on every diagonal, so every stem grows at the fastest rate (a pumpkin every 4 tries). An observer over each stem fires the four pistons over its fruit cells; the squeezed pumpkin drops into a hopper minecart under the mud, and a hopper line under each pair of rows carries it to a chest (8 chests). Needs open sky or light 9 at the stems. The carts go in with the rail trick (rail, cart, break the rail). 2112 iron. Copies side by side every 17 blocks.

Full-size sugar cane farm, 204 canes on a 16x16 field: water on every fifth cell of a lattice (x + 2z = 0 mod 5) gives every cane exactly one water neighbour; mud under the canes and a hopper under every cell and under a one-cell ring around the field (the lattice continues into it, so edge canes keep their water) catch every item. A downward piston above each cane breaks its 2nd block; all 204 fire at once through a carpet of dust on the piston tops, fed from both sides by two repeater lines, on each pulse of one 30 s hopper clock (hopclk-sealed-p600, inverted by a torch into a short pulse). The hopper rows carry the items to two collector columns, each into its own chest. 96% of the plant ceiling at vanilla speed.

Full-size sugar cane farm swept by one flying machine, 192 canes on a 10x24 field: the same water lattice, hopper floor and ring as the piston farm, but no piston per cane. A 6-block two-way flying machine (two halves of observer, slime and sticky piston that push and pull each other one block every 10 ticks) runs the length of the field at the canes' 2nd-block height with a wing on each half (slime with a stone blade under it, 4 columns a side) and destroys every 2nd block it passes. A station at each end (an observer that sees it arrive, the stone it powers, dust behind the leading piston) sends it back, so it shuttles for ever, 438 ticks a round trip; it starts when the cane under its first observer is planted. Its slime launches the items it touches along the track, so walls past both ends, a curb along the sides, a catcher row and a pocket behind each station's dust bring every item to the hoppers; two collectors, two chests. 94% of the plant ceiling at vanilla speed.
